extracted.intended_audience: The people of the State of New York / general readers of the 1787 ratification debate
extracted.subtask_description: A series of late-18th-century political essays arguing in favor of the proposed federal Constitution and the advantages of union over smaller republican or pure-democratic forms. It explains principles for structuring government to limit faction, secure liberty, and promote national security and commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: regular_distribution_of_power_into_distinct_departments
rubrics_metrics.description: The regular distribution of power into distinct departments is an improvement of modern political science and a means by which the excellences of republican government may be retained and its imperfections lessened or avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Listed as one of several modern improvements (along with legislative balances and checks, independent judges, and representative legislature) that reduce the vices of republican government; presented as an institutional design criterion to prevent tyranny and anarchy.
Original phrasing: "The regular distribution of power into distinct departments; the introduction of legislative balances and checks; the institution of courts composed of judges holding their offices during good behavior; the representation of the people in the legislature by deputies of their own election... These are means, and powerful means, by which the excellences of republican government may be retained and its imperfections lessened or avoided."

rubrics_metrics.name: legislative_balances_and_checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce legislative balances and checks to prevent concentration and abuse of power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Provided together with separation of powers and judicial tenure as a modern improvement; recommended as an instrument to ameliorate the defects of popular governments and reduce instability and injustice.
Original phrasing: "the introduction of legislative balances and checks... these are means, and powerful means..."

rubrics_metrics.name: judicial_independence_via_good_behavior_tenure
rubrics_metrics.description: Instituting courts composed of judges holding their offices during good behavior to secure impartial administration of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Presented as a key structural safeguard against faction and executive/legislative encroachment; part of the catalogue of modern improvements that help retain republican excellences.
Original phrasing: "the institution of courts composed of judges holding their offices during good behavior..."

rubrics_metrics.name: representation_by_elected_deputies
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation of the people in the legislature by deputies of their own election (a representative republic rather than a pure democracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Framed as central to refining public views and controlling faction: representatives can better discern national interest and resist local, factious temptations (though they can also be corrupted). The essay contrasts republic (representation) with pure democracy.
Original phrasing: "the representation of the people in the legislature by deputies of their own election..."

rubrics_metrics.name: enlargement_of_the_orbit_as_remedy_for_faction
rubrics_metrics.description: The enlargement of the orbit (increasing the size/extent of the political unit or consolidating smaller states into a confederacy) ameliorates the imperfections of popular systems by suppressing faction and increasing security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Argues that extending the sphere of republican government is a modern discovery improving political stability; applied both to enlarging a single state and consolidating several states into a confederacy; used as a principal argument in favor of the proposed Union.
Original phrasing: "the ENLARGEMENT of the ORBIT within which such systems are to revolve... either in respect to the dimensions of a single State or to the consolidation of several smaller States into one great Confederacy."

rubrics_metrics.name: utility_of_a_confederacy
rubrics_metrics.description: A confederacy can suppress faction, guard internal tranquility, and increase external force and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Supported by historical practice and writers; confederacy is defended as competent to combine advantages of republican internal happiness with monarchical external force; quotations from Montesquieu used to show confederate republics are an expedient for extending popular government.
Original phrasing: "The utility of a Confederacy, as well to suppress faction and to guard the internal tranquillity of States, as to increase their external force and security, is in reality not a new idea."

rubrics_metrics.name: confederate_republic_definition_and_discretion_of_federal_authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A confederate republic is an assemblage of societies (two or more states) into one; the extent, modifications, and objects of federal authority are matters of discretion so long as member states retain separate organization for local purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Used to counter fears that a union necessarily abolishes state governments; argues that representation in Senate and reserved state powers make the proposed Constitution consistent with a federal (confederate) model.
Original phrasing: "The definition of a CONFEDERATE REPUBLIC seems simply to be 'an assemblage of societies,' or an association of two or more states into one state. The extent, modifications, and objects of the federal authority are mere matters of discretion."

rubrics_metrics.name: two_methods_of_curing_faction
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two methods of curing the mischiefs of faction: (1) removing its causes; (2) controlling its effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Presented as the fundamental dichotomy for addressing faction. The essay proceeds to analyze both approaches and to reject removal of causes as impracticable or worse (destroying liberty or forcing uniformity).
Original phrasing: "There are two methods of curing the mischiefs of faction: the one, by removing its causes; the other, by controlling its effects."

rubrics_metrics.name: removal_of_causes_impractical_and_unwise
rubrics_metrics.description: Removing the causes of faction would require destroying liberty or making every citizen identical in opinions/interests, both impracticable or worse than the disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Used to reject the first method of cure; liberty is essential and cannot be abolished to suppress faction; diversity of faculties and property ensures persistent causes of faction.
Original phrasing: "There are again two methods of removing the causes of faction: the one, by destroying the liberty which is essential to its existence; the other, by giving to every citizen the same opinions... It could never be more truly said than of the first remedy, that it was worse than the disease."

rubrics_metrics.name: relief_only_by_controlling_effects_of_faction
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the causes of faction are inherent and cannot be removed, relief must be sought by controlling its effects through institutional design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Leads to argument for representative government and an extended sphere to make majority-oppression or concerted faction more difficult.
Original phrasing: "The latent causes of faction are thus sown in the nature of man... The inference to which we are brought is, that the CAUSES of faction cannot be removed, and that relief is only to be sought in the means of controlling its EFFECTS."

rubrics_metrics.name: republic_better_than_pure_democracy_for_controlling_faction
rubrics_metrics.description: A republic (representative government) can cure mischiefs of faction in ways a pure democracy cannot: by delegating government to a chosen body and by extending the sphere of the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Explains two great differences — delegation to representatives and larger number/sphere — and shows how they refine public views, make corrupt elections harder, and increase options for fit choices.
Original phrasing: "A republic, by which I mean a government in which the scheme of representation takes place... The two great points of difference between a democracy and a republic are: first, the delegation of the government... secondly, the greater number of citizens, and greater sphere of country..."

rubrics_metrics.name: representation_refines_and_enlarges_public_views
rubrics_metrics.description: Delegation of government to elected representatives refines and enlarges public views by passing them through a chosen body whose wisdom and patriotic sentiments better discern the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Also acknowledges the risk of corruption or local prejudice among representatives; the criterion is thus to design representation to maximize refinement and minimize corruption.
Original phrasing: "The effect of the first difference is... to refine and enlarge the public views, by passing them through the medium of a chosen body of citizens, whose wisdom may best discern the true interest of their country..."

rubrics_metrics.name: larger_republic_reduces_probability_and_effect_of_factional_majorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Extending the sphere and increasing the number of citizens brings greater variety of parties and interests, making it less probable that a majority will share a common motive to oppress others and more difficult for them to concert and execute oppressive plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Central justification for union: the Union's greater variety of parties and larger scale increases security against faction by impeding concert and reducing uniformity of motives.
Original phrasing: "Extend the sphere, and you take in a greater variety of parties and interests; you make it less probable that a majority of the whole will have a common motive to invade the rights of other citizens... the extent of the Union gives it the most palpable advantage."

rubrics_metrics.name: balance_number_of_representatives_against_local_knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a mean: representatives must be numerous enough to guard against cabals but limited enough so they remain acquainted with local circumstances; the federal Constitution's division (national for aggregate interests, state for local) is a happy combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Design criterion about representative size and allocation of competences between national and state legislatures to balance local and national concerns.
Original phrasing: "It must be confessed... there is a mean, on both sides of which inconveniences will be found to lie... The federal Constitution forms a happy combination in this respect; the great and aggregate interests being referred to the national, the local and particular to the State legislatures."

rubrics_metrics.name: confederate_council_may_influence_internal_adminstration_example
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical practice (e.g., Lycian confederacy) shows confederate councils sometimes appointed judges and magistrates of member cities, indicating confederacies can and have exercised internal influence over members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Used to rebut strict distinctions that a confederacy must avoid internal administrative concerns; offers precedent showing practical exceptions and that absolute rules do not govern confederacies.
Original phrasing: "In the Lycian confederacy... The COMMON COUNCIL had the appointment of all the judges and magistrates of the respective CITIES. This was certainly the most delicate species of interference in their internal administration..."

rubrics_metrics.name: federal_navy_and_unified_commercial_policy_as_external_advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: A continued Union under efficient government enables coordinated commercial policy and the establishment of a federal navy, which increase bargaining power with foreign nations and protect commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Argument that a united America can negotiate better commercial privileges, exclude foreign carriers, and, with a federal navy, exert influence in European and West Indies affairs; used as a practical advantage of union beyond internal faction control.
Original phrasing: "By prohibitory regulations, extending, at the same time, throughout the States, we may oblige foreign countries to bid against each other... A further resource... would arise from the establishment of a federal navy."

rubrics_metrics.name: prevent_concert_of_majority_by_number_and_local_situation
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent a majority faction from succeeding, render the majority (even if united by a common passion) unable — by their number and dispersed local situation — to concert and carry into effect schemes of oppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Design implication: structure representation and the geographic/constitutional reach so that numbers and dispersion make coordinated oppression difficult.
Original phrasing: "Either the existence of the same passion or interest in a majority at the same time must be prevented, or the majority... must be rendered, by their number and local situation, unable to concert and carry into effect schemes of oppression."
